## a plan repair is never refused

ID: `ship/a-plan-repair-is-never-refused`

Status: **implemented and tested**

When the planning gate would refuse (no package, or a package the validator rejects), `scripts/ship.py` SHALL still let the branch proceed when every file it changes since its merge base with the default branch is a planning or documentation file (under `docs/`, `wiki/` or `planning/`, or any `*.md`), and SHALL print that it did so. A branch that changes any other file SHALL be refused as before. The exception repairs, never breaks: ship SHALL also run the planning gate on the merge base, and when the base passes it SHALL refuse the branch (the branch would make a compliant package fail; issue #261).

## a record only change is never refused

ID: `ship/a-record-only-change-is-never-refused`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/ship.py` SHALL treat a file under `cases/`, `results/` or `raw/` as upkeep for "An upkeep-only change is never refused", so a branch that only adds or changes a run's record (its case folder, result files, captured sources) merges without the planning package gate. A branch that also changes any file outside those folders, the documentation rule and the model/lock rule SHALL be refused as before. Ship's printed line SHALL name the record-only folders.

## add on gates switch off from the copier answers

ID: `ship/add-on-gates-switch-off-from-the-copier-answers`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/ship.py` SHALL read the keys `ship_planning_gate` and `ship_one_page_plans` from `.copier-answers.yml` on the default branch at `origin` (never from the branch being shipped, so a branch cannot turn its own gate off), reading each as a top-level `key: value` line. When a key's value is `false` (any letter case), ship SHALL skip that gate (the whole planning gate with its plan-repair and upkeep exceptions, or the one-page-plan check) and print and log `ship: planning gate: off (.copier-answers.yml ship_planning_gate: false)` or `ship: one-page plans: off (.copier-answers.yml ship_one_page_plans: false)`. A missing file, a missing key or any other value SHALL leave the gate on. The prior-art check is core and has no switch.

## an upkeep only change is never refused

ID: `ship/an-upkeep-only-change-is-never-refused`

Status: **implemented and tested**

When the planning gate would refuse (no package, or a package the validator rejects), `scripts/ship.py` SHALL still let the branch proceed when every file it changes since its merge base with the default branch is upkeep: a planning or documentation file as in "A plan repair is never refused", a lock file (`uv.lock`, `package-lock.json` and the like), or a file whose added lines equal its removed lines once model names (and, in dependency manifests, version numbers) are masked, with at least one name or version really changed. Ship SHALL print that the branch is upkeep only and how many files it changes. A branch that changes any other file, or adds or deletes a file outside the documentation rule, SHALL be refused as before. The classification is the one Company Planning's validator uses for package freshness.

## answer the plan content question for the push hook

ID: `ship/answer-the-plan-content-question-for-the-push-hook`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/plan_content.py --repo R --base B --head H --validator V` SHALL answer whether the commits from B to H change plan content, using the same function `ship` uses, so the push hook and `ship` decide alike. It SHALL exit 0 and print a line starting `skip:` when nothing changed, and exit 1 with a line starting `validate:` when plan content changed or anything is uncertain: B is not a commit, H is not the checkout's HEAD, or the validator has no `freshness()`.

## check every one page plan a merge adds or changes

ID: `ship/check-every-one-page-plan-a-merge-adds-or-changes`

Status: **implemented and tested**

A one-page plan is a `.md` file committed under `docs/plans/` that carries the line `Plan size: small`. Text inside a fenced code block is a quotation, not the page's own: the marker line, the headings and the read line count only outside code blocks. Before the planning gate and the check run, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL check every one-page plan that the merge (from the merge base with the default branch to HEAD) adds, changes or renames, whatever characters its file name holds; when no merge base is found it SHALL check every committed one-page plan. A one-page plan is complete when it has the five headings `## Goal`, `## How Brian judges it`, `## Cost and time`, `## Scoring fixed beforehand` and `## What already exists`, at most 150 lines, and a line that starts `Independent read: <YYYY-MM-DD>, pass` with a real date; when the page has more than one line that starts `Independent read:`, the last one counts. A page that starts with a byte-order mark or holds bytes that are not UTF-8 SHALL be checked, not skipped. ship SHALL refuse the merge, with nothing pushed, when a page it checked is not complete, naming the page, each thing it lacks and the rule; no exception for a plan repair or an upkeep-only change SHALL let that page merge. For each complete page it SHALL print and log one line naming it. Under this requirement ship SHALL not refuse a merge for a plan page that lacks the line `Plan size: small`, for a one-page plan the merge does not touch, or for one the merge deletes.

## every planning gate run is recorded

ID: `ship/every-planning-gate-run-is-recorded`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Each time ship runs one of its two planning gates it SHALL append one JSON line to `planning-verdicts/<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl` beside the day's ship log, holding `time`, `repo` (owner/name from origin), `branch`, `head`, `gate`, `mode`, `outcome` (`pass`, `warn`, `refuse`, `unavailable` or `off`), `reason` (the refusal text, or null) and `log` (the day's ship log). A record that cannot be written SHALL NOT stop the merge; the day's log SHALL say so.

## hold a new repository to a deployed plan

ID: `ship/hold-a-new-repository-to-a-deployed-plan`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/ship.py` SHALL treat a repository as new when its earliest first commit (`git log --max-parents=0 --format=%cI`) is dated on or after 2026-11-05. A new repository with no planning package and no complete one-page plan SHALL be refused, naming the company-planning:planning-compliance skill. A new repository with a package SHALL also be listed in the plan list: the file `plan_list_path:` names on `origin/main` of the checkout `plan_list_checkout:` names (Requirement: settings-come-from-config; fetched first, a failed fetch leaving the last fetched list), matched on the repository name of its clone URL, so its review page deploys; if it is not listed, ship SHALL refuse and print the exact line to add. When that list cannot be read, ship SHALL refuse and say why. Each refusal names the rule.

## keep its own lane when the caller still needs it

ID: `ship/keep-its-own-lane-when-the-caller-still-needs-it`

Status: **implemented and tested**

When given `--keep-lane`, or when the environment has `SHIP_KEEP_LANE=1`, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL, after the pull request reads back MERGED, run the lane sweep for its repository without removing its own lane (passing it to `scripts/lane_sweep.py` as `--keep-lane`, which keeps that lane with the reason `kept by --keep-lane`), and SHALL print and log `ship: kept this lane (--keep-lane); the periodic sweep removes it once idle`. The repository's other finished lanes SHALL still be removed. Without the flag, ship SHALL remove its own lane as before.

## limit how many checks run at once

ID: `ship/limit-how-many-checks-run-at-once`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/ship.py` SHALL take one of `$SHIP_CHECK_SLOTS` (default 3) machine-wide check slots before it sets up the environment and runs the check, and SHALL hold it until the check ends. A slot is a file lock under `$SHIP_STATE_DIR/check-slots`, so a run that dies frees it. A run that finds every slot taken SHALL print which repositories hold them, wait up to `$SHIP_SLOT_WAIT` seconds (default 1800), and then stop with exit status 1 and nothing pushed. A slot count of 0 SHALL turn the limit off. A run that skips its check because the tree already passed SHALL take no slot.

## merge only the commit whose check passed

ID: `ship/merge-only-the-commit-whose-check-passed`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/ship.py` SHALL run the repository's check (default `make check`, or `--check`) on a clean tree, and push and merge only when it exits 0. The merge SHALL be pinned to the checked commit (`gh pr merge --match-head-commit`), the pull request merged SHALL be one that is open for the branch (a merged one is never reused), and the run SHALL succeed only when the pull request reads back as MERGED. Every step prints its exit status and time, and the whole run is appended to one log file per day.

## merge with a method the repository allows

ID: `ship/merge-with-a-method-the-repository-allows`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Before the check, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL read which merge methods the repository allows (`gh repo view --json mergeCommitAllowed,rebaseMergeAllowed,squashMergeAllowed,viewerDefaultMergeMethod,defaultBranchRef`) and whether its default branch requires linear history (branch protection `required_linear_history` or an active ruleset rule of type `required_linear_history`); linear history rules out `merge`. It SHALL merge with `--method` when that method is allowed, else with the repository's default method when allowed, else with the first allowed of rebase, squash, merge, and SHALL print and log each replacement of `--method`. When no method is allowed it SHALL stop with exit status 1 before the check and push nothing. When the settings cannot be read it SHALL use `--method`, else `merge`, and say the settings were unreadable (a branch that is not protected, or protection that cannot be read without admin rights, is not a refusal).

## planning gates are set in lockstep yaml

ID: `ship/planning-gates-are-set-in-lockstep-yaml`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`ship` SHALL read `planning.gate` (the planning-package gate) and `planning.one_page_plans` (the one-page-plan check) from `lockstep.yaml` on the default branch at `origin`, never from the branch being shipped. Each SHALL be `block`, `warn` or `off`, a bare YAML `true` meaning `block` and `false` meaning `off`; an absent file, section or key SHALL mean `warn`. A gate SHALL be off when either this setting or the `.copier-answers.yml` key says off, and the printed and logged line SHALL name the file that said so (`ship: planning gate: off (lockstep.yaml planning.gate: off)`). Under `warn`, a plan verdict (a validator rejection, a missing planning package, an incomplete one-page plan or a plan-list refusal) SHALL print and log `ship: warning: <gate>: <reason>; not refused (lockstep.yaml planning.<key>: warn)` and the merge SHALL go on, while a validator that cannot be fetched or cannot run SHALL still refuse. Any other value SHALL refuse the merge naming the value, with nothing pushed. The prior-art check has no switch.

## prepare a fresh worktree s environment before the check

ID: `ship/prepare-a-fresh-worktree-s-environment-before-the-check`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Before running the check, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL run `uv sync --all-extras` when the repository top has a `uv.lock` or `pyproject.toml`, no `.venv`, and the check is a `make` command (the repository's own Makefile check, which the default `make check` is), and `npm ci` when it has a `package-lock.json` and no `node_modules`. Each step that runs SHALL be a logged step, and a nonzero exit SHALL stop the run with nothing pushed and SHALL remove the `.venv` or `node_modules` that the failed step created. An environment that is already present SHALL be left alone.

## rebase a branch that is behind the default branch before checking it

ID: `ship/rebase-a-branch-that-is-behind-the-default-branch-before-checking-it`

Status: **implemented and tested**

After refusing a dirty tree and before the gates and the check, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL fetch `origin` and, when the default branch (`origin/HEAD`, else `origin/main`) is not an ancestor of HEAD and the branch is not on the remote, rebase the branch onto the default branch, then check and merge the rebased commit. A repository's `.gitattributes` merge drivers apply to this rebase, so a file marked `merge=union` keeps the lines both sides added. When the rebase stops on a conflict it SHALL abort the rebase, leave the branch at its earlier commit, refuse the merge with nothing pushed, and name the conflicting paths. When the branch is already on the remote, or the fetch fails, it SHALL print and log one line saying it did not rebase and why, and go on.

## refuse a branch whose hidden acceptance run failed or is out of date

ID: `ship/refuse-a-branch-whose-hidden-acceptance-run-failed-or-is-out-of-date`

Status: **implemented and tested**

After it has caught up with the default branch and before it runs the check, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL read every readable `summary.json` under `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/lockstep-runs/<repository>/` (the main checkout's folder name) whose `branch` is the branch being shipped or whose `head` is a commit reachable from HEAD and not from the default branch; an unreadable one SHALL be skipped with a printed warning. When there is at least one, ship SHALL refuse the merge with nothing pushed, naming `lockstep accept check <change>` as the way to record a new run, unless the newest by run id has `accept.exit` 0, a positive integer `accept.passed`, zero `accept.failed` and `accept.errors`, `uncommitted` 0, and `head` equal to HEAD as it will be merged (so a branch that was rebased must be checked again). With none, ship SHALL print and log `ship: no hidden-test run recorded for this branch` and go on; a run made by another user or under another `XDG_STATE_HOME` is not found, which this message makes visible. Missing or malformed acceptance counts SHALL refuse a matching record, including a record rewritten after ship's own rebase. A legacy record with valid exit, pass, failure and error fields may omit the skipped count.

## refuse a merge whose openspec change lacks a prior art record

ID: `ship/refuse-a-merge-whose-openspec-change-lacks-a-prior-art-record`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Before the planning gate and the check, `ship` SHALL run Lockstep's prior-art check (`src/lockstep/prior_art.py`, the file beside ship's own module) with `--repo` set to the repository and `--files` set to every file under `openspec/changes/` that the merge (from the merge base with the default branch to HEAD) adds or changes; when no merge base is found it SHALL run it without `--files`. When the merge adds or changes no file under `openspec/changes/` it SHALL run nothing and print and log one line saying so. It SHALL refuse the merge, with nothing pushed, when the check exits 1, showing what the check printed. When the check file is missing it SHALL refuse the merge and say to reinstall `ship`; when the check exits with any status other than 0 or 1 it SHALL refuse the merge, show the exit status and say this is not a verdict on the record. When the check exits 0 it SHALL print and log its summary line.

## refuse a new repository with no planning package

ID: `ship/refuse-a-new-repository-with-no-planning-package`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Before running the check, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL refuse, with nothing pushed, a repository whose first commit is on or after 2026-11-05 and that has neither `docs/planning/planning-package.json` nor a complete one-page plan (requirement "Check every one-page plan a merge adds or changes"), naming the rule, the one-page plan and the company-planning:planning-compliance skill, and naming what each incomplete one-page plan lacks. A new repository with no package and at least one complete one-page plan committed under `docs/plans/` SHALL proceed: ship SHALL print and log one line naming the page, and SHALL not read the plan list. For this it reads every committed one-page plan, whether or not the merge touches it; a page git does not track does not count. A repository whose first commit is earlier SHALL merge with a printed warning that names the rule and the skill. It applies only when ship merges in that repository; ship SHALL start no agent for it.

## refuse a planning package the validator rejects

ID: `ship/refuse-a-planning-package-the-validator-rejects`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Before running the check, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL look for `docs/planning/planning-package.json`. When it exists, ship SHALL run Company Planning's `validate_planning_package.py` on it, read from `origin/main` of the company-planning repository (`$SHIP_COMPANY_PLANNING`, default `~/code2/company-planning`, fetched first), and stop with nothing pushed unless the validator exits 0 or fails only for age (below). This holds however old the repository is. When the validator cannot be fetched or run, ship SHALL stop, and SHALL say it could not run, which is not a verdict on the package. ship SHALL run the validator under a fixed interpreter that imports its packages (`jsonschema`, `pydantic`), never under ship's own python, which is a project's venv when a caller such as `uv run scripts/release.py` runs ship: the first of `/usr/bin/python3` and `uv run --no-project --with jsonschema --with pydantic python` that imports both, or the command line in `$SHIP_VALIDATOR_PYTHON`. A validator that dies on an import error SHALL stop ship as "could not run", without the `--no-freshness` rerun. When the validator rejects the package, ship SHALL run it once more with `--no-freshness`; when that run exits 0, the package failed only for its age, so ship SHALL print a warning that names the out-of-date package and proceed.

## settings come from config

ID: `ship/settings-come-from-config`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Where the plan list lives SHALL be read when it is needed: from `$SHIP_PERSONAL_VPS` and `$SHIP_PLAN_LIST` when set, else from the top-level `plan_list_checkout:` and `plan_list_path:` keys of `graph-config.yaml` beside the project graph (found as requirement `the-project-graph-is-named-in-lockstep-yaml` says). When either is not named, a new repository with a package SHALL be refused with a message naming both keys; nothing is pushed. No other run reads them.

## skip a check that already passed on the same tree

ID: `ship/skip-a-check-that-already-passed-on-the-same-tree`

Status: **implemented and tested**

After the check exits 0 on an unchanged tree, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL append the tree hash (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`), check command, repository, head and time to `~/.local/state/ship/passed.jsonl` (folder overridable by `$SHIP_STATE_DIR`). Before running the check, when an entry has the same tree hash and check command, ship SHALL skip the check and print and log `ship: check skipped: tree <hash> already passed`<cmd>`at <time> (head <sha>)`. `--recheck` SHALL run the check regardless. A failed check SHALL record nothing.

## the project graph is named in lockstep yaml

ID: `ship/the-project-graph-is-named-in-lockstep-yaml`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`ship` SHALL find the project graph, whose folder holds `graph-config.yaml`, from `$PROJECT_GRAPH` when set, else from `planning.project_graph` in `lockstep.yaml` on the default branch at `origin` (never from the branch being shipped), else from `~/code2/aes-config/PROJECT_GRAPH.json`. When it reads the plan list it SHALL print and log `ship: project graph: <folder> (<source>)`, the source being `$PROJECT_GRAPH`, `lockstep.yaml planning.project_graph` or `default`. The value SHALL be a local path to a `.json` file starting with `~` or `/`; any other value (a git address, a relative path, a folder) SHALL be named by the side-file check and SHALL be a plan-list refusal at merge time, naming the value.

## validate the planning package only when the merge changes plan content

ID: `ship/validate-the-planning-package-only-when-the-merge-changes-plan-content`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Before running the validator, `scripts/ship.py` SHALL ask whether the merge (from the merge base with the default branch to HEAD) changes plan content. Plan content SHALL be what the validator's freshness check counts, read by calling the validator's own `freshness()` with the merge base as the reviewed revision, never a second list in ship; a change to `docs/planning/planning-package.json` itself SHALL also count. When the merge changes no plan content, ship SHALL not run the validator and SHALL print and log one line saying it skipped the validator and why. When it changes plan content, ship SHALL validate as before. When the answer cannot be had (no merge base, a validator without `freshness()`, an error), ship SHALL validate. Checking the merge base for a plan repair SHALL always validate. The new-repository rules SHALL apply as before: a new repository with no package is refused, and one with a package must be on the plan list.
